title: Longest Subarray with Equal 0s and 1s
question: Given an array, find the longest subarray with equal number of 0s and 1s.
explanation: The entire array has 3 zeros and 3 ones, so the whole array (length 6) is the longest valid subarray.
notes: Treat 0 as -1, then find the longest subarray with sum 0 using prefix sum + hashmap.

title: Trapping Rain Water
question: Given n non-negative integers representing an elevation map where the width of each bar is 1, compute how much water it can trap after raining.
explanation: Utilize two pointers to calculate trapped water between the left and right maximum heights.
notes: Approach: left max and right max arrays; or two-pointer at both ends.

title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array
question: Given a sorted array, remove the duplicates in-place such that each element appears only once and return the new length.
explanation: Your function should return length = 2, with the first two elements of nums being 1 and 2 respectively.
notes: Use two-pointer technique: one slow pointer for unique elements, one fast pointer for scanning.

title: Maximum Sum of Subarray of Size K
question: Given an array of integers and a number k, find the maximum sum of a subarray of size k.
explanation: Subarray [5, 1, 3] has the maximum sum of 9.
notes: Classic sliding window problem - compute initial window sum, then slide by adding next, removing previous.

title: First Non-Repeating Character
question: Given a string, find the first non-repeating character in it and return its index. If it doesn't exist, return -1.
explanation: 'l' is the first character that appears only once, at index 0.
notes: Use a frequency map (or array of 26) in two passes.

title: Valid Palindrome
question: Given a string, determine if it is a palindrome, considering only alphanumeric characters and ignoring cases.
sampleInput: A man, a plan, a canal: Panama
explanation: After removing non-alphanumeric characters and ignoring case, the string reads the same forward and backward.
notes: Use two pointers from both ends, skipping non-alphanumeric characters.

title: Spiral Matrix
question: Given an m x n matrix, return all elements of the matrix in spiral order.
explanation: Traverse the matrix in a clockwise spiral: top row → right column → bottom row → left column, shrinking boundaries each time.
notes: Maintain 4 boundaries (top, bottom, left, right) and shrink them after each pass.

title: Rotate Image (Clockwise 90)
question: Given an n x n matrix, rotate it 90 degrees clockwise in-place.
explanation: Rotate the matrix 90 degrees clockwise. The element at [0][0] moves to [0][n-1].
notes: Transpose the matrix, then reverse each row.

title: Three Sum
question: Given an array of integers, find all unique triplets that sum to zero.
notes: Sort the array, then fix one element and use two pointers for the remaining two.

title: House Robber
question: Given an array of non-negative integers representing the amount of money of each house, determine the maximum amount you can rob tonight without alerting the police (adjacent houses cannot be robbed).
notes: DP transition: dp[i] = max(dp[i-1], dp[i-2] + nums[i]).

title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
question: Given an unsorted array of integers, find the length of the longest increasing subsequence.
explanation: The longest increasing subsequence is [2, 3, 7, 101], length 4.
notes: O(n log n) using patience sorting with binary search, or O(n^2) with DP.

title: Rotting Oranges
question: Given a grid where each cell has value 0 (empty), 1 (fresh orange), or 2 (rotten orange), every minute a fresh orange becomes rotten if it is adjacent to a rotten one. Return the minimum minutes until all oranges rot, or -1 if impossible.
notes: Multi-source BFS starting from all rotten oranges simultaneously.
